structure:
Part 8 of repo:tests, "animals e2e: whole journeys and reference-list content". It read, in full, the 7 flat specs under tests/animals/e2e/journeys (README.md, save-and-continue.spec.ts, back.spec.ts, back-entry-points.spec.ts, pet-cats-air-permanent-address.spec.ts, horse-temporary-admission.spec.ts, poultry-rail-transit.spec.ts, promoted-notification.spec.ts) and the 5 specs under tests/animals/e2e/features/reference-lists (country-of-origin-list, destination-country-list, transit-country-list, port-of-entry-list, port-of-exit-list), together with the support code those specs drive: page-objects/animals/{index,overview-page,origin-of-import-page,consignment-details-page,arrival-details-page,transited-countries-page}.ts, page-objects/shared/{journey-checks,type-ahead,base-page}.ts, domain/animals/constants/{country-codes,point-of-entries,journey-options,means-of-transport}.ts, flows/animals/{journey,seed-form-steps,seeded-journey}.ts, flows/shared/journey-context.ts, fixtures/{ui,seed-context}.ts, the whole resources/reference-data folder (reference-data.ts, paths.ts, countries.json, countries-origin.json, ports-of-entry.json) and docs/animals-journey.md. For wording the reference-list specs assert it also read domain/animals/constants/{origin-page,import-reason-page,transit-countries-page,consignment-addresses-page,import-reasons,internal-market-purposes,certification-purposes,transporters,commodity-lines,journey-commodity-line-answers}.ts and utils/{transit-countries-assertions,playwright/environment}.ts as context.

Layout of the slice: the journeys folder holds three kinds of spec. save-and-continue.spec.ts (3 describes, 8 test declarations) proves the page order Save and continue follows, what it skips and where an incomplete notification lands. back.spec.ts (2 describes, 6 tests) and back-entry-points.spec.ts (1 describe, 2 tests) prove where Back lands from each entry point. Four whole-journey specs each walk one consignment end to end through flows/animals/journey.ts: pet-cats-air-permanent-address.spec.ts (1 test), horse-temporary-admission.spec.ts (1 test, @cross-browser), poultry-rail-transit.spec.ts (1 test) and promoted-notification.spec.ts (1 test, @compose). The reference-lists folder holds 12 tests across 5 specs, every one skipped unless the run targets the compose stack, each asserting the first option and the whole option list of one select against the captured reference-data fixtures.

Counts: 32 literal test() declarations across the 12 specs (save-and-continue 8, back 6, back-entry-points 2, the four journey specs 1 each, country-of-origin 2, destination-country 4, transit-country 2, port-of-entry 1, port-of-exit 3), which run as 34 tests because the country-of-origin and transit-country specs each generate their list test twice, once with JavaScript on and once off. Covered: every test by its title, the four whole journeys as an ordered walk with the answer given at each page, the Save-and-continue page order and the page it skips by means of transport, the Back rule from every entry point the two Back specs drive, and for each of the five reference lists where its entries come from, the entries, the order and the first-option wording. Gaps recorded where the slice is silent: docs/animals-journey.md carries no journey page list to compare against, no whole-journey spec walks the transporter-add pages, the party edit pages, delete or cancel-amend, no whole-journey spec is a germinal-products one, and the reference-list specs assert no hint or placeholder wording.

claims.statement: The animals journey tests drive the live-animals notification wizard through the browser front door rather than through any API or seeded shortcut.
claims.quote: These tests walk the notification wizard (`AnimalsJourney`, `flows/animals/journey.ts`) via the front door.

claims.statement: A journey test is held to validating a complete flow through the application from the user's perspective, not an individual component or isolated feature.
claims.quote: A journey test (sometimes called a user journey test or end-to-end journey test) is a type of automated test that focuses on validating a complete flow through an application from the user’s perspective, rather than testing individual components or isolated features.

claims.statement: A trader starts a new live-animals notification from the notification dashboard's "Create new notification" button and lands on the origin page, whose address already carries the new notification's reference number.
A live-animals notification's pages all sit under the live-animals set base at /notifications/<reference>/<page slug>, and the overview is that path with no slug.

A journey page's address carries the places the trader came by as a `from=` query parameter, newest last and comma-separated, and the three recognised starting places are the overview, the dashboard and the INS.
claims.note: mechanism: the trail query the suite reads and writes to prove where Back goes; it works on the list of places already visited, not on any answer.

claims.statement: The suite proves a cattle-by-air notification can be taken through every task with Save and continue, from creating it to submitting it, and runs that walk on every supported browser.
claims.quote:
'walks a cattle-by-air notification through every task with Save and continue, from create to submitted',
    { tag: '@cross-browser' },

claims.statement: The cattle-by-air walk answers the pages in this order: origin of import, what are you importing (species), main import reason, commodity details, identification details, additional details, arrival details, transport details (transporter), upload documents, consignment addresses (five parties then CPH), contact address.
An air consignment's Save and continue goes straight from arrival details to the transporter list: the transit countries page is not offered.
A road consignment's Save and continue goes from arrival details to the transit countries page.
The means of transport a trader can choose are Air, Rail, Road and Sea.

The declared Save-and-continue order from the main import reason to the end of the journey is: main import reason, commodity details, identification details, additional details, arrival details, transit countries, transporter, upload documents, consignment addresses, contact address.
claims.quote:
/** The pages Save and continue goes through from the main import reason to the contact address, in order, starting at `first`. */
  saveAndContinueStopsFrom(first: SaveAndContinueStop): SaveAndContinueStop[] {
    const stops: SaveAndContinueStop[] = [
      this.animalsPages.importReason,
      this.animalsPages.consignmentDetails,
      this.animalsPages.animalIdentification,
      this.animalsPages.additionalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.arrivalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.transitedCountries,
      this.animalsPages.transporter,
      this.animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments,
      this.animalsPages.addresses,
      this.animalsPages.contactAddress,
    ];
claims.note: The order the suite holds the journey to; the per-page specs in other parts assert it page by page, and this part's journey specs walk subsets of it.

claims.statement: Each Save and continue press carries the page just left onto the trail, so the next page's address lists every place already saved, newest last.
Pressing Save and continue on the contact address, the last page of the journey, lands the trader on that notification's review page.
claims.quote:
const referenceNumber = await animalsJourney.walkCattleByAir(document);
      await expect(pages.page).toHaveURL(animalsPages.notificationView.expectedUrlPattern(referenceNumber));

claims.quote: 'walks a pet-cats-by-air notification from create to submitted, with a mixed permanent-address choice and every task complete'

claims.quote:
/** Each animal that needs one answers the permanent address page with either option. */
export type PermanentAddressAnswer = { origin: 'placeOfDestination' } | ({ origin: 'newAddress' } & NewPermanentAddressFields);

claims.statement: A new permanent address asks for a name or organisation name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, phone and email, with address line 2 and county optional.

The review's addresses card lists each animal's permanent address against a row named by the species' common name and the animal's number, such as "Domestic Cat 1" and "Domestic Cat 2", showing the place of destination for the first and the typed address for the second.
claims.note: The row's name comes from reference data's common name for the commodity, read live from the reference-data API, not from a fixture.

claims.statement: The permanent address page is reached from the consignment addresses page, and for the cats walk that happens between the five parties being added and the page being left.
claims.quote: It answers the permanent address page from the consignment addresses page, which the walk reaches only inside `walkFromTransporterToReview`, so the caller's permanent-address step is supplied to that method rather than run before or after it.

claims.statement: The suite proves a live-animals notification started from the INS notification-type question can be submitted all the way through, and runs that proof only against the compose stack.
claims.quote:
'submits a promoted live-animals notification through the hub-owned spine',
  { tag: '@compose' },

claims.statement: A submitted notification ends at the live-animals set's /notifications/<reference>/confirmation page, headed "Import notification submitted", with the reference number shown in the confirmation panel.
The submitted-notification walk gives only the answers the frontend requires, so every page it answers is a page a trader cannot skip.
claims.quote: `submitNotification` gives only the answers the frontend requires (`MANDATORY_ANSWERS`), unless the caller passes a fuller set such as `ALL_ANSWERS`.

claims.statement: The answers a live-animals notification must carry to be submitted are: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is needed, at least one commodity line, main import reason, purpose in the internal market, what the animals are certified for, whether unweaned animals are included, five parties, a CPH number, an arrival date, a point of entry, a means of transport, a transport identification, a transport document reference, a transporter and a contact address.
claims.note: The type is written so that a missing required answer is a compile error (journey-options.ts:51-55).

claims.statement: The answers the frontend leaves optional are the region of origin code (asked only when the origin needs one), the internal reference, the transited countries (asked only of rail and road consignments) and an accompanying document.
A region of origin code is given exactly when the origin needs one: giving a code without needing one, or needing one and giving none, is a contradiction the suite refuses to drive.
claims.quote:
/** Throws when the answers contradict each other: a region code is given exactly when the origin requires one. */
export const assertConsistentAnswers = (answers: NotificationAnswers): void => {

claims.statement: Five parties are answered on the consignment addresses page, in this order: Consignor, Place of destination, Place of origin, Consignee, Importer; the contact address is a sixth party answered on its own page.
claims.quote: export type PartyRole = 'placeOfOrigin' | 'consignor' | 'consignee' | 'importer' | 'placeOfDestination' | 'contact';

claims.statement: A party picker refuses an address-book record that does not carry the role being answered.
claims.quote: Every name must match a record `flows/shared/address-book-seed.ts` seeds holding that role, since a picker now refuses a record that does not carry its own role.

claims.statement: A party is only committed to the notification by a server round trip after its radio is ticked, so leaving the picker before that round trip keeps the previously saved party.
claims.quote: `selectAndCommit` (`page-objects/animals/party-picker-page.ts`) ticks a party's radio, then re-searches to commit it: the picker only threads its checked party through a server round trip, so a link off the page before that round trip carries the previously-saved party, not the just-ticked one.
claims.note: mechanism: how the picker threads the chosen party through the form post; it works on the picker's own checked state, not on a page the trader sees.

claims.statement: The expected reference-list content is read from fixtures copied from the animals frontend's own capture of reference data, not written by hand in the tests.

claims.statement: A country select's search behaves as a plain contains-the-typed-text match, ignoring case.

A reference-list field is an accessible autocomplete that enhances a native select of the same name: with JavaScript off the trader uses the select itself, and with it on the trader types and picks a suggestion, which is announced in a live region and shows the matching letters in bold.
The autocomplete carries a search button with an icon of its own, and a hint beneath the field's label.

The country of origin and transit country searches are placeheld "Search for a country", while the import reason's selects are placeheld and open on "Select one" and the port of entry on "Select a port".

claims.note: The reference-list specs assert only the first option text, never the placeholder or hint; the placeholders are recorded here from the constants they share with other parts' specs.

claims.statement: The notification reference number and a status tag are shown in a journey strip at the top of every notification page.
An amendment in progress can be cancelled from the journey strip or from the page body, both labelled "Cancel amend".

A draft notification can be seeded through the frontend's own forms as far as three stages: origin and commodity answered (which opens the other tasks), on through arrival, or every section answered so the draft can be declared.

The pages a seeded draft posts to, in order, are: origin, commodities (a search then the species), consignment-details, commodities/identification, import-reason, additional-details, the five party selects, permanent-address when needed, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries when given, transporters and consignment/contact/select.
claims.ref: flows/animals/seed-form-steps.ts:104-207 (commoditySteps, consignmentSteps, addressSteps, arrivalStep, transportSteps, contactStep, seedSteps)
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's own seeding path through the frontend's form posts; it works on the notification's stored answers, and the page slugs it names are the journey's real URL slugs.

claims.statement: Declaring a notification is a two-step post to the declaration page, carrying a concurrency token taken from the review page, and ends in a redirect to the confirmation page.
Declaring an unfinished draft is refused, and the trader is sent back to the review with refused=1 in the address.
Cancelling an amendment returns the trader to the review with cancelled=1 in the address, and deleting a notification returns with deleted=1.
A notification created with no answers at all lands on its origin page, and that is what a POST to the notifications path redirects to.
claims.quote:
export const CREATE_PATH = `${SET_BASES.liveAnimals}/notifications`;
export const CREATED_AT_ORIGIN = new RegExp(`^${CREATE_PATH}/(?<referenceNumber>[^/?]+)/origin${OPTIONAL_RETURN_AND_TRAIL_PATTERN}$`);

claims.statement: A notification cannot be seeded with an accompanying document: a document only reaches a notification through a browser upload.
A notification cannot be seeded as far as the review through the API, so any test that needs a review walks the whole journey in the browser.
claims.quote: The API seed unlocks only origin and commodity, so a spec that needs the review walks the whole journey rather than seeding it. The walk's addresses leg picks the canned parties whose names and countries a review assertion reads.

claims.statement: Every notification a test creates is recorded against the test run, so a failure names the notification it was working on.
A trader is signed in before any journey page is reached, and an identity with more than one organisation must pick one.

The journey walks the whole way through only where the services the walk depends on are reachable: the suite starts the origin page from a sign-in and, for the promoted-notification walk, only against the compose stack.
The transporter list saves through unfilled, so a journey can pass the transport details page without choosing a transporter.
claims.quote: `reachTransporterFromHub` goes back to the transporter list from the hub within a journey that is already unlocked. The page saves through unfilled. Arrival details are filled on the way because the default means, Road, keeps transited countries in scope, and transit countries are answered next.

claims.statement: The transporter list shows only the newest address-book entry of each name, and saving the list is refused with "Select a transporter from the list" when the entry the list chose has since been replaced.
claims.quote: Every test signs in to the same organisation, and its transporter list shows only the newest address-book entry of each name. When two tests add a transporter of the same name at once, the later add replaces the entry the earlier test's list chose, and that list's save is refused with "Select a transporter from the list".

Several animals on one commodity line are identified one at a time, each saved before the next, with "Save and add another" then "Save and finish", and each saved animal is listed as a row.
A horse is additionally identified by its name, which the other species are not asked for.
The unweaned-animals question is only asked of some consignments: the walk answers it only when it is on the page.
A page the trader opens from the overview and leaves with "Save and return to overview" returns to the overview, so a task can be answered without walking the rest of the journey.

The journey's page order exists only in code, in saveAndContinueStopsFrom and the two overview task-row constants.

Why the animals flows and page objects are written the way they are. The code carries no comments, so the reasons live here. Sections without a file name are steps of `flows/animals/journey.ts`.

claims.note: Every notification page object resolves to the live-animals set base, and the promoted-notification spec names the live-animals set outright, so nothing in this slice proves a second sibling set end to end.

claims.note: The type-ahead page object offers a hint locator (page-objects/shared/type-ahead.ts:22-24) and the constants carry placeholders, but no reference-list test reads either.

claims.statement: Only the country of origin and transit country lists are proven with JavaScript off and by typing into the search: the destination country, port of entry and port of exit lists are proven only as selects, with JavaScript on.

claims.statement: No journey spec proves the wording of a question page's caption, hint or body copy along the walk: the whole-journey specs assert only the pages' headings, by locator, and the values shown on the review afterwards.
claims.note: The per-page specs in other parts carry the page-level copy assertions; a look-and-feel change to a question page would not be caught by anything in this slice.

claims.statement: Nothing in this slice proves what the dashboard looks like or offers beyond three actions it uses: searching for a reference, Resume on a draft, and View or Amend on a submitted notification.
claims.note: The journeys only pass through the dashboard; the dashboard's own content is another part's.
